info.name: Lepara Ale fele Moya API
info.description:
Every endpoint of the Lepara Ale fele Moya API, grouped like the API documentation (/api/docs).

1. Set the collection variable `baseUrl` (default `http://localhost:3000/api/v1`; for the live API, `https://<your-render-service>.onrender.com/api/v1`).
2. **Admin:** run "Admin: sign-in → Sign in with username and password", then "Sign in with a code from the authenticator app" with the 6-digit code from your app. `adminToken` is saved for every admin request.
3. **Customer:** run "Customer accounts → Sign in". `customerToken` and `refreshToken` are saved for the customer requests.
4. Access tokens last 15 minutes: run the matching "Get a new access token" request when you get `TOKEN_EXPIRED`.

IDs in the URLs (`:id`) are examples: change them to real ones from the list requests. Query parameters are listed but switched off; tick the ones you want.

item.name: Track a request, application or pledge

request.description: The reference number and the last 4 digits of the phone number given on the form. A wrong reference and wrong digits get the same 404, so nobody can find out which references exist. The reply holds no personal details. Only wrong attempts count: 5 per 15 minutes.

item.name: Product cards for the Shop screen
One product page, with each size's availability

request.description: Keep each size's `variantId`: the cart and orders use it.
A 6-digit code is emailed. An email that already has an account gets exactly the same reply (the email itself tells the owner to sign in instead), so nobody can find out who has an account.

item.name: Send a new sign-up or login code

request.description: `{ email }` for a new sign-up code, or `{ pendingToken }` for a new login code. At most one code a minute (429 with the seconds to wait) and 5 an hour per email.

item.name: Confirm the email with the code: signed in

request.description: Replies with a session. The mobile app (no `Origin` header) gets `refreshToken` in the reply and keeps it in expo-secure-store; the website gets it as an httpOnly cookie instead.

Replies with a session, or `{ twoFactorRequired: true, pendingToken, expiresIn }` when the customer turned on login codes (then call /auth/login/verify). An unconfirmed email gets 403 `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED`, only after the right password. Five wrong passwords lock the account for 15 minutes (423).

item.name: Turn emailed login codes on or off
Finish signing in with the emailed login code

request.description: The app sends `{ "refreshToken": "..." }`; the website sends nothing (the cookie is used, with `credentials: "include"`). The refresh token is replaced every time: always save the new one. Using an old one again ends every session of that customer.
A new email shows as `pendingEmail` until the code sent to it is entered at POST /me/email/verify.

item.name: Confirm the new email with its code
Change the password (signs out other devices)

request.description: Replies with a new session for this device; every other device is signed out and the customer is emailed.

item.name: Email a code to reset the password

request.description: The same reply whether or not the email has an account.

item.name: Choose a new password with the emailed code

request.description: Every device is signed out; sign in again with the new password.
Personal details are removed and every device is signed out. Past orders are kept for the financial records.
Prices come from the database only: any price or total in the request is ignored. A line that can't be ordered as asked has a `problem` to show under it; the quote never fails because of one.

header.description: A new UUID for each order. Send the same key again when retrying, and the first order is returned (with the header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`) instead of a second one being placed.

request.description: Checked and priced again inside one transaction, with the sizes locked, so stock can't be oversold. EFT orders start as Pending payment, with the order number as the bank reference; cash on delivery starts as Confirmed. A line that can't be ordered gets 409 naming the item and how many are left. At most 3 unpaid orders open per customer.

item.name: My orders, newest first (the Orders tab)
One of my orders, with its tracking steps
Cancel an unpaid order before it is packed

request.description: The stock goes back. A paid order gets 409 asking the customer to contact the NGO for a refund.

item.name: Register this phone for push notifications

request.description: Call on every app start (after asking for permission) and after signing in or out. `token` is the native token from expo-notifications' `getDevicePushTokenAsync()`, not an Expo push token. Signed in (with the Authorization header), the phone also gets that customer's order updates; without it, news only.

item.name: Sign in with username and password (step 1 of 2)

request.description: The reply says what comes next. A new admin first sets up an authenticator app (`two_factor_setup`); after that, every sign-in asks for a code from the app (`two_factor_verify`). Five wrong passwords lock the account for 15 minutes (423).

item.name: Start setting up the authenticator app

request.description: Show the QR code (`qrCodeDataUrl`) for the admin to scan with Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator, or let them type the `manualEntryKey`.

item.name: Confirm the authenticator app with its first code: signed in

request.description: Replies with a session and 10 backup codes, shown only this once. The refresh token is set as an httpOnly cookie (`lepara_admin_refresh`), never in the reply.

item.name: Sign in with a code from the authenticator app (step 2 of 2)

request.description: A 6-digit code from the app, or one of the backup codes (each works once). Each app code works only once.

item.name: Get a new access token with the refresh cookie

request.description: Call with `credentials: "include"` so the browser sends the cookie. The cookie is replaced on every refresh; using an old one again ends every session of that admin.

item.name: Change your password (required after a temporary one)

request.description: Every other session of this admin ends. Replies with a new session (and a new refresh cookie).
Replies with a temporary password, shown only here. At first sign-in the new admin sets up 2FA, then must choose their own password.
`isActive: false` deactivates the admin and ends their sessions at once. The last active super admin can never be removed (409).

request.description: The quantity can only change through a donation, a fulfilled request or an adjustment (sending `quantityOnHand` gets 400).

item.name: Adjust stock by hand (damaged, recount), with a reason
Give out goods for an approved request

request.description: The request must be Approved; it becomes Fulfilled. All items are taken in one transaction: if any is short, nothing is taken and the reply is 409 naming the item and how many are left. Send `{ "items": [] }` when the help was not goods.

`type: "Monetary"` needs `amount` (rands); `type: "Goods"` needs `stockItemId` and `quantity`, and adds that quantity to stock. `initiativeId`, `receiptReference`, `isAnonymous` and `dateReceived` (default today, never in the future) are optional.

item.name: Void a donation recorded by mistake

request.description: Donations are never deleted. Voiding a goods donation takes its quantity back out of stock; if some of the goods were already given out, the reply is 409.

item.name: Record an accepted pledge as received

request.description: The pledge must be Accepted; it becomes Received and a donation is recorded (goods also go into stock). The donor is emailed a thank-you.

item.name: Record an EFT payment (confirms the order) or cash collected

request.description: `amount` (rands) must equal the order total, otherwise 400. `reference` is the bank statement reference (the order number if left empty). A paid order is emailed and notified.

One step at a time: Confirmed → Packed → Shipped (needs `courierReference`) → Delivered; skipping or going back gets 409. Cancelling needs a `reason` (sent to the customer) and is allowed until shipped; a paid order also needs `refunded: true`. The stock goes back on cancelling.
